newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH SHARES MIXED, UPSIDE SEEN THIS WEEK.
newsitem.headline: POLISH SHARES MIXED, UPSIDE SEEN THIS WEEK.

text.p: Polish shares were mixed on Tuesday but analysts said the higher turnover and stronger buying after price-fixing and at continuous trade signalled more gains later this week.

Analysts said such gains, led by relatively undervalued small-cap stocks, could lead overall market growth even if the U.S. FOMC meeting later on Tuesday raises the Funds rate by the expected 25 basis points, which may have been priced in.
"I think the market will rise tomorrow even if rates in America go up," said Czeslaw Pospieszynski, an analyst at Bank Gdanski brokerage.
The main market's all-share WIG index fell 0.2 percent to 16,163.2 points and turnover rose 45.6 percent to 185.2 million zlotys on all three markets.

Analysts said large initial public offerings next month could draw capital from listed stocks but that buying of small-cap issues especially by smaller domestic investors might spur overall market growth this week.

"Large-cap firms have risen a lot recently...and it's not expected they'll have big real earnings growth this year, while a lot of smaller firms can have a real-term growth of 15 to 20 percent," said Sebastian Buczek of ING BSK Asset management.
Analysts said top gainer Espebepe rose 10 percent, extending Monday's 8.1-percent surge, after last week's steep fall as speculators played on the uncertain future of the debt-ridden builder.
Mostostal Zabrze jumped seven percent after Monday's news that Germany's Adam Opel AG, a General Motors unit, confirmed it would award Mostostal a 90 million mark contract, analysts said.
NFI units rose one percent at the regular session and fell 0.6 percent in continuous trade, where most stocks rose. -- Steven Silber +48 22 653 9700
